test_title: PYST 52: RRB Group D - GS (Held On: 21 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: What conclusion can be drawn from the microscopic observation of onion peel cells?

options.text: The size of the onion decides the shape of its individual cells
All onions are made up of similar small structures called cells
Onion bulbs contain different cell types for different functions
Each onion peel contains cells of different composition

solution:
The correct answer is __**All onions are made up of similar small structures called cells**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The microscopic observation of **onion peel** (the **epidermis**) demonstrates that all onions, regardless of their **size**, **shape**, or **variety**, are composed of basic structural units known as **cells**. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• When an onion peel is examined under a **compound microscope**, it reveals a pattern of **rectangular** or **brick-shaped** compartments arranged in a regular fashion, each containing a **nucleus** and **cytoplasm**.
 
• The **size** of the onion bulb does not affect the **shape** or **size** of these individual cells; a large onion and a small onion will both show identical-looking cellular structures under magnification. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• The **onion peel** is a **homogenous tissue** layer (the **protective epidermis**), meaning the cells within this specific layer are very similar in **composition** and **function**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• While an entire **onion plant** has different cell types for different functions (such as **root cells** or **vascular cells**), the specific observation of the **peel** primarily highlights the **uniformity** of the **dermal tissue** rather than a diversity of functions. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Structure of an Onion Cell:** As a typical **plant cell**, an onion cell contains a **rigid cell wall** made of **cellulose**, which provides **structural support**. It also features a large **central vacuole** that maintains **turgor pressure** and pushes the **nucleus** to the **periphery**.
 
• **The Role of Staining:** Because most cell organelles are **transparent**, stains like **Safranin** or **Iodine solution** are used. These **chemicals** color the **nucleus** and **cell wall** more intensely, making them clearly visible under **light microscopy**.
 
• **Cell Theory:** The observation of onion cells is a fundamental piece of evidence for the **Cell Theory**, formulated by **Matthias Schleiden** and **Theodor Schwann** in **1838-1839**. This theory states that **all living things** are made of **cells** and cells are the **basic unit of life**.
 
• **Historical Context:** The term "cell" was first coined by **Robert Hooke** in **1665** after observing **cork**. Later, in **1831**, **Robert Brown** discovered the **nucleus** within the plant cell, which is easily seen in onion peel preparations.
 
• **Onion Bulb Botany:** The **onion** (***Allium cepa***) is a **modified underground stem** called a **bulb**. The "peels" we observe are the **epidermal layers** of the fleshy **leaves** that store **food** and **nutrients** for the plant.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Experimental Procedure:** To observe these cells, a thin **transparent membrane** is stripped from the **concave side** of an onion fleshy scale. It is placed in a **watch glass** with **water** to prevent **dehydration** or **folding**.
 
• **Mounting:** The specimen is mounted on a **glass slide** with a drop of **glycerin** (to prevent drying) and covered with a **coverslip**. It is vital to avoid **air bubbles** during this process for a clear **microscopic view**.
 
• **Magnification:** Typical classroom observations use a **low-power objective** (**10x**) for a wide field of view and a **high-power objective** (**40x**) to see the **nucleus** and **cell boundaries** in detail.
 
• **Biological Classification:** Onions are **monocotyledons**, and their cells are often used in labs because they are large, easy to extract, and provide a **single-layer** view of **eukaryotic** architecture.
